To make it easier for you to see what’s coming up at your Columbus Recreation and Parks Department, some exciting changes are coming to this newsletter!

Beginning in November, you’ll receive the newsletter every Thursday evening so you can plan for the coming week – don’t worry, we’re making the newsletter shorter so it will be easy to skim and pull out what’s important to you.

As you read the new format, tell us what you think! Send your feedback to ColumbusRecParks@Columbus.gov.

Rallying to Keep Our Parks Clean

Monday, Columbus Recreation and Parks partnered with Columbus Crew and Ohio Blind Soccer for a litter cleanup at Rhodes Park. Volunteers and staff from all three organizations spend two hours picking up litter. This was a great way to work with volunteers and community partners to keep our parks beautiful!

With the increased traffic in parks, preventing litter is a year-round effort that will take all of us. Here are some easy ways you can prevent litter:

  1. Set a good example. Always throw trash and recycling in a proper receptacle.
  2. Take your trash with you. With the increased in park visitors, trash cans are filling up quickly. Keep a litter bag in your car and hang on to litter until you find a trash can.
  3. Encourage others to not litter. Remind others about the proper way to dispose or trash and recycling, and report littering.

New Center Managers Here to Serve the Community 

Community centers serve a critical role in neighborhoods across the City, connecting you with activities, resources - and each other!

With some recent retirements, five centers have new managers. Some are familiar faces while others are new to the center, or the department.

For more information, visit the Theatre page.

Help Shape the New West Case Road Park

Columbus Recreation and Parks is developing a new 58-acre park at the historic sheep farm located at 2425 West Case Road. The site will become one of the major greenspaces in northwest Columbus and has a wide range of possibilities—from sports to hiking to nature to special programming—all within a short walk of more than 6,000 residents. 

To ensure the new park meets the needs of residents, we want your input! Complete this brief survey to tell us what you want to see. If you haven’t been to the site, join us Oct. 16 for a walking tour and envision what’s possible!

Learn more about the project, and sign up to receive email updates!

Make a Difference in Your Community This Holiday Season

 If you, your family, business or organization is looking for a way to give back this holiday season, please consider our Adopt a Center program. It’s convenient, easy and makes a difference.

The Adopt a Center program provides gifts and meals that are distributed through an event at community centers. Last year, 6,300 meals were served, and more than 2,800 children received gifts, thanks to the generosity of nearly 600 individuals and 30 organizations/businesses.

Celebrate, Learn About Nature’s Dynamos at Pollinator Field Day

Pollinators–such as birds, bees and butterflies–are important to our environment and world. They pollinate trees, flowers and crops; plants that provide our food and food and shelter for other animals. Did you know that pollinators are responsible for one out of every three bites of food?

Celebrate nature’s dynamos at free Pollinator Field Days in September and October! There’s something for all ages, including kids’ activities, a pollinator habitat scavenger hunt and a butterfly catch-and-release–we’ll learn how to tag monarchs if we catch any. We’ll try out the free iNaturalist app to identify and document the flowers and pollinator species we see. You can also volunteer to help with habitat restoration efforts. Events are outdoors and COVID-19 safety protocols will be followed. Walk-ins are welcome–register online to volunteer. It’s sure to be a day of fun and learning!

Free Leadership Development Program for 6-8th Graders

The City Leaders program develops the leaders of tomorrow so our children stay here and serve as the future leaders of Columbus. Conservation Volunteer Program

This past April we launched a new volunteer program focusing on conservation efforts. Pam Steck works on the Parks Maintenance team and has been leading volunteer conservation events. Her favorite part of working with volunteers is teaching them something new about nature and conservation.

When asked what her favorite volunteer experience was she said, "My first volunteer event was with a group, they were great people to work with, but several of them were uncomfortable about walking in tall vegetation in the Whetstone prairie. At one point the group created an assembly line, one person would cut the curly dock and then pass it to the next person and the next until the volunteer at the end of the line collected the flowers in a bag for disposal. By the end of the event, everyone had been in the prairie working, and I could see how proud the originally uncomfortable volunteers were with themselves for venturing into the tall vegetation."

Pam started her conservation career by volunteering with Columbus Recreation and Parks Department, where she helped removed honeysuckle at Lou Berliner Sports Park! If you would like to join Pam at future conservation volunteer events, check out the links below!

  • 9/11: Conservation Event at Scioto Southland
  • 9/25: Conservation Event at Glenwood Park
  • 10/16: Conservation Event at Big Run Park

Columbus Gives Back is a volunteering-focused nonprofit organization, emphasizing giving back to Columbus but also fostering connectedness with and among volunteers. Their mission is to provide social volunteer and philanthropic opportunities  to create a culture of community engagement to connect people to central Ohio. Columbus Gives Back continues to be a collaborative partner, with five volunteer projects scheduled for this season alone. Thank you, Columbus Gives Back!

For more information, please call Columbus Division of Water, Watershed Management Section at 614-645-1721.

Volunteers Needed: Soccer League

Soccer season is quickly approaching, and we are looking for volunteer coaches to help our young athletes learn, improve and enjoy the game of soccer. The weekly time commitment is 3-4 hours/week, with games being on Saturdays. Contact Char Barnes, Recreation Administrative Manager of Youth Sports, for more details.

Volunteers Needed: United for Girls

Columbus Recreation and Parks Department has been chosen to be a part of U.S. Soccer Foundation's United for Girls Cohort. According to the Women's Sports Foundation, girls drop out of sports by the age of 14, which is two times the rates of boys. Girls of all ages participate in sports less than boys, with greater disparities for girls living in under-served communities. Only 27 percent of coaches for youth leagues are women. Girls and women who play sports have greater confidence and self-esteem. Unfortunately, many girls are left out of the game. This is an amazing honor, and we are excited to learn the best way to provide the next generation of girls with the opportunity to succeed on and off the field. We want to increase opportunities for youth girls to play soccer as well as the number of female coach-mentors leading them. Would you consider coaching? We would love to have you!

The time commitment will be 3-4 hours per week with practices starting at the end of August. The season will run from Sept.11 - Oct.16. Contact Char Barnes, Recreation Administrative Manager of Youth Sports, for more information.

Partnering to Conserve Our Environment 

Parks serve an essential role in improving the quality of life for residents. Parks benefit our residents and community by providing a place for residents of all ages and abilities to connect with nature, which benefits our mental and physical health; protecting our environment by cleaning the air and water, replenishing aquifers, reducing stormwater runoff and safeguarding wildlife habitat; and strengthening our economic well‐being by conserving energy and resources

Columbus Recreation and Parks works to conserve and protect our parks, greenspaces, trees and wildlife. In addition to maintaining 19 nature preserves and 33 pollinator gardens, last year we removed 94,000 bags of trash from parks, spread 35 pounds of prairie seed and planted nearly 1,000 trees.

Be an advocate for your parks and environment-join our conservation efforts!

In April, we launched a volunteer conservation program focused on pollinator planting, invasive removal, litter cleanup and stream restoration. This season, volunteers have assisted with a creek cleanup at Holton Park, honeysuckle removal and litter cleanup at Academy and Wolfe Park, prairie maintenance at Whetstone and much more.

If you’re interested in joining us for an upcoming conservation project, sign up online, or contact Betty Blockinger, volunteer services manager, at BKBlockinger@columbus.gov.

Stay Engaged and Active This Fall: Register for Activities

The end of summer doesn’t have to mean the end of fun! Columbus Recreation and Parks offers activities for all ages and interests throughout the year. From arts and crafts to fitness, sports and senior activities, there’s something for everyone.

We’re gearing up for fall programming, and registration opens in just a few short weeks for the following activities:

  • Creative arts classes: Activities offered by the Cultural Arts Center (CAC) begin Sept. 7. Registration opens Aug. 28 at 8:30 a.m.; register online or in person at 139 E. Main St., 43215.
  • Swim lessons, water fitness and more: Activities at the Columbus Aquatics Center begin Sept. 20. Registration opens Sept. 7 at 9 a.m.; register online or in person at the Columbus Aquatics Center, 1160 Hunter Ave., 43201.
  • Community center-based, adaptive sports and outdoor recreation activities: Activities for 50+ begin Sept. 13; all other activities begin Sept. 14. Registration for all other activities begins Sept. 7 at 12:30 p.m.; register online or in person at your neighborhood community center.
  • Sports leagues and tournaments: Play goes well into the fall! Explore options and register online.

Keep the fun going and engage with your community this fall with Columbus Recreation and Parks programming! Browse the many options available and sign up.

Columbus Symphony Brings Free Concerts to Parks

Whether you’re a long-time fan of the symphony or have been meaning to experience your first performance, Columbus Symphony (CSO) and Columbus Recreation and Parks have a great opportunity for you!

This month, the CSO is partnering with Columbus Recreation and Parks to bring free concerts to parks across the city. These “Columbus Symphony Community Concerts” are 45-minute, live orchestra performances that feature a mix of symphonic and pops music, including pieces from Elgar, Sousa, and Tchaikovsky as well as “Highlights from The Lion King,” “Best of the Beatles,” “Michael Jackson Hit Mix” and more. Concerts include:

  • Aug. 18, 6:30 p.m. – Driving Park*
  • Aug. 19, 6:30 p.m. – Marion Franklin Park
  • Aug. 20, 6:30 p.m. – Dodge Park*
  • Aug. 21, 6:30 p.m. – Mayme Moore Park*

*A small ensemble of Urban Strings’ youth orchestra will perform a 'pre-concert' from 6-6:20 p.m.

Admission is free! Bring your blankets and chairs and pack a picnic. See you at the symphony! The show will go on rain or shine! 

Photo credit: Stephen Pariser

Get a Head Start on Your Plans for Holiday Giving

While summer isn’t officially over, Columbus Recreation and Parks is gearing up for the holidays!

Many residents still are facing financial difficulties made worse by the pandemic. And, with cases on COVID-19 on the rise and the spread of the Delta variant, there are likely to be more families in need this holiday season.

For the second year, the department will partner with generous groups, organizations, business and individuals to make the holiday season brighter for those in need through the Adopt a Center program. Sponsors ‘adopt’ a community center and provide gifts and meals that are distributed at a group meal, holiday party or other community event. Last year, 6,300 meals were served and more than 2,800 children received gifts, thanks to the generosity of nearly 600 individuals and 30 organizations/businesses.

There are opportunities for individuals, work teams, organizations and companies to participate, no matter your budget:

  • Make a financial donation: Donations will be used to purchase toys, food and other needed items for children and families.
  • Purchase an item for a family or child in need: Visit our Amazon Wish List and purchase an item for a family in need. Items will be delivered directly to the City of Columbus for distribution.
  • Adopt a community center: If your company or organization can help in a big way, we are looking for sponsors to provide financial or in-kind donations to fill a wide variety of needs for the community surrounding the center. 

To learn more, visit crpfoundation.org/adoptacenter or contact Erika Shemberg at EJshemberg@columbus.gov.

Fresh and Exciting Changes Coming to Many Playgrounds 

This is a big year for our playgrounds!

Many playgrounds across the city are getting updates in 2021. Improvements vary by park and could include upgrading some of the equipment and adding rubberized surfaces. Celebrating How Parks, Recreation Make Our Community Great

July is National Park and Recreation Month. This annual event, hosted by the National Recreation and Park Association, celebrates the positive impact recreation and parks departments have on communities across the country.

This year's theme, Our Park and Recreation Story, celebrates the history of departments. And at 111 years old, Columbus Recreation and Parks has quite a rich history! Did you know: 

  • Established on July 15, 1910, the City Recreation Department enriched Columbus by finding ways to make streets, alleys, boulevards, parks and public grounds more beautiful. On Jan. 2, 1972, the City Recreation Department merged with the Division of Forestry and Parks to become the Columbus Recreation and Parks Department.
  • The City features two skate parks. Dodge Skate Park, our first skate park, is 16 acres and features three all-concrete bowls; 3, 4, and 6 feet deep. The 4-foot bowl can function as a half-pipe, while the 6-foot bowl has an intense "verte." The park was designed by Frank Hawk, legendary skateboarder Tony Hawk’s father.
  • You can enjoy the outdoors at more than 400 parks across the City. One, English Park (also known as the Children's Africentric Playground), is home to the Kwanzaa Playground. The park focuses on positive African-American images based around the concept that "it takes a whole village to raise a child." The park was renovated in 2014 with new play equipment and art restoration as well as a new portal by artist Queen Brooks. Learn more about our parks.
  • Residents from preschool to age 99+ can access programs catering to a variety of interests including the arts, fitness and educational pursuits. Many are low- or no-cost, and all are designed to help residents connect with nature, wellness and creativity-and each other! One program, City Leaders, is celebrating its 10th anniversary, and introduces middle school students to the leaders and locations that make Columbus great. It educates middle school youth to become model citizens and future leaders of our City. Explore all current recreational opportunities.

You, our residents, are what brings our story to life! We want to hear how you have engaged with us over the years. Share your photos and memories on social media by using the hashtag #OurParkAndRecStory and tagging us.

Help Keep our Parks Beautiful

Columbus is home to more than 400 parks, where residents can work out, relax and engage with nature year-round. During the pandemic, our parks have been a place for residents to safely get outside and spend time with family and friends, and traffic in parks has significantly increased.

Unfortunately, littering also has increased in our parks.

Littering sometimes is unintentional, such as when something falls out of your bag without you knowing. But most littering is done intentionally, often because people are lazy or careless, don’t want to wait to find a trash can or see other litter and follow suit.

A study by Keep America Beautiful found the most littered items include cigarette butts, food wrappers, plastic bottles, disposable cups, grocery bags, straws, beverage cans, and tire and vehicle debris.

Preventing litter isn’t just about keeping our parks beautiful, it’s about protecting our health and the environment. Here’s how litter affects our world:

  • Litter causes pollution as it degrades and releases chemicals and microparticles. For example, cigarette butts can contain chemicals such as arsenic and formaldehyde that make their way into the soil and water.
  • Litter can kill wildlife. Researchers estimate that over 1 million animals die each year after ingesting or becoming entrapped in litter.
  • Litter facilitates the spread of disease. Litter is a breeding ground for bacteria and diseases, and can spread diseases, viruses and parasites. 

YOU can help prevent litter! Here are some easy ways:

  1. Set a good example. Always throw trash and recycling in a proper receptacle.
  2. Take your trash with you. With the increased traffic in parks, trash cans are filling up quickly. Keep a litter bag in your car and hang on to litter until you find a trash can.
  3. Encourage others to not litter. Remind others about the proper way to dispose or trash and recycling, and report littering.
  4. Volunteer to clean up a park. Sign up for a volunteer shift to clean up and beautify your favorite park. Learn more about our volunteer program.

Our parks enhance the quality of life for all of our residents. Please, help keep our parks beautiful!

Helping Families Access Nutritious Food

Access to adequate, healthy food is key to the overall health and development of children, and to helping families achieve their best. Columbus Recreation and Parks Department's Food Office continues to help residents access free meals and fresh produce. 

According to Feeding America’s most recent data, its 2019 Map the Meal Gap Study, 165,000 Franklin County residents do not have access to sufficient and nutritious foods. This has been made worse by the pandemic, and more families are facing food insecurity for the first time.

The Food Office’s two signature program provides meals and fresh produce to help address this critical need:

  • Go, Lunch!: This Summer Food Program offers free, nutritionally balanced meals during the summer months at community centers along with other various locations. Last summer, more than 472,000 meals were served at over 230 locations in the Columbus area. These meals are served to anyone between the ages of 1–18. Find a location near you.
  • Free Mobile Produce Markets: These markets offer families a week’s worth of free produce. These drive-thru markets are staffed by volunteers wearing masks and gloves who load the produce directly into the trunk or car. Simply drive in, drive up and drive off! Markets are held most Thursdays and Fridays, February through December. See when we are in or close to your neighborhood.

This is a time when many Columbus residents may find themselves in need of additional support. Columbus Recreation and Parks is here to help. If you need assistance, stop by one of the sites. If you know someone who needs assistance, share this information with them.

Visit www.golunch.club to learn more.

“But He Looks Hungry!” Why it’s Best to NOT Feed the Wildlife

Going to the park and feeding the ducks and geese sounds like a lot of fun–and the animals seem to love the tasty treats! But did you know that feeding human food to wildlife is actually harmful and potentially deadly?

This article from the National Park Service explains how feeding wildlife presents several hazards for wildlife, including increasing their chances of being injured and causing health issues that can be fatal. Feeding wildlife human food also increases their scat (waste)!

Please, next time you’re at a park, do not feed the wildlife! You’re making the safe choice for our animal friends.

New Exhibit Features Artists’ Take on Getting Through the Pandemic

Join us June 4–July 10 in the Cultural Arts Center’s Main Gallery for The Art of Surviving a Pandemic. This exhibit features local invited artists who tell their stories about how they continued to work during the COVID-19 pandemic through a variety of art forms including visual, poetry, performance and music. 

Works focus on questions we’ve all been wrestling with–where did their inspirations come from? Did they learn new techniques? Did they have to cope with the loss of loved ones? The exhibit is curated by Leticia Vazquez-Smith, President of the Latino Arts for Humanity.

The Cultural Arts Center galleries are open Mondays 1-4 p.m. and 7-10 p.m., Tuesdays–Thursdays 9 a.m.-4 p.m. and 7-10 p.m., and Fridays-Saturday 9 a.m.-4 p.m.  Register for a visit online or by phone at 614-645-7047.

Help Shape the New Columbus Community Sports Park

As the Columbus Crew prepares to move downtown, our community has a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to shape 25 acres of new green space, park space and recreational programming on the near-northeast side of the City.

The Columbus Community Sports Park will be a new, centrally-located park and recreation space that will benefit nearby neighborhoods, the City and the region. It will provide much-needed access to park and recreation space to the 200,000 residents who live within 3 miles of the site. Facilities, fields and green space will be easily accessible to neighborhoods including: Milo Grogan, Weinland Park, Linden, North Columbus, Glen Echo, Indianola Trace, University District, Clintonville and others.

The Columbus Community Sports Park will be located on the grounds of the historic Crew Stadium and adjacent to the Ohio State Fairgrounds along Interstate 71, between East 17th Avenue and Hudson Street.

The Community Sports Park has two primary components. The first is facilities for organized – formal – sports programs. These will be available for rent by families, local teams, traveling leagues and others. These could include multi-use wood courts, tournament-level synthetic turf fields, indoor field space, meeting rooms, classrooms, a rock climbing wall, a concessions area or covered outdoor pickleball courts.

The second is informal sports and community park spaces, which will be available at no cost to residents and teams. These could include mixed-use grass fields, basketball courts, walking and bicycling trails with exercise stations, green space with an outdoor courtyard or plaza, open shelters, picnic tables, a playground, a splash pad or a skate park.

Earth Day events looked a little different for Columbus Recreation and Parks Department this year. Check out a video of the tree planting we had at Lou Berliner Sports Park this year: here.

The department also hosted a series of smaller pollinator habitat planting events. Volunteer groups seeded native pollinator species, including goldenrod, milkweed and purple coneflower. These gardens will serve as habitat that provides food and shelter for the pollinators. Pollinators are animals like bees, butterflies and bats that move pollen from one plant to another. Increasing pollinator habitats across more than 400 parks is an ongoing project within the department. You can visit a variety of settings without leaving Columbus. How many of the City’s 400 parks can you explore this summer?

Looking for some unique, handmade gifts? Look no further than Golden Hobby Gift Shop!

Golden Hobby Shop will reopen June 1 at its new location in the Columbus Performing Arts Center (CPAC). For 50 years, this senior arts and consignment shop has offered an array of handmade goods for sale, including quilts, ceramics, woodcrafts, paintings and more. The artists will have access to studio space at the facility, along with organizational and material support, helping them hone their craft. item.title: Columbus Recreation and Parks - January News and Events
item.description:
Outdoor Winter Fun

There is plenty to see and do outdoors, no matter the season!

Getting outdoors in the winter is good for your mental and physical health. You’ll get some physical activity while soaking up some extra vitamin D, something that’s challenging during gray Ohio winters! The natural light, physical activity and mental engagement can lift your mood and energy levels.

Here are some fun ways to get outside this winter:

Take a winter hike: Take a hike on one of Columbus’ trails. With nearly 220 miles of trail, there’s a lot to explore!

Explore nature: Check out what lives and grows in the winter by exploring the great outdoors. Download the free iNaturalist app to help identify your finds. Add some fun by creating a scavenger hunt for your family, or host a virtual event with a larger group to engage with others in a safe way!

Visit a park: Go for a walk, host a winter picnic or enjoy the many amenities at your local park. Check out a list of our parks online. With nearly 400 parks, chances are you’ll find one around the corner that’s new to you!

Sign up for a guided activity: Looking for something more structured? Sign up for a variety of outdoor activities, including guided hikes and park clean up events, with our Outdoor Recreation team. Our safety protocols will ensure you’ll have fun and meet new people in a safe environment!

It’s important to stay safe outside! Be sure to dress for the weather – dress in layers made of wool or synthetic fabrics, and keep your head, hands and feet warm. Check out these tips from our partner REI for more information. Also, follow health and safety guidelines – practice social distancing, clean your hands often with soap and water or hand sanitizer and stay home if you’re not feeling well.

Keep Your Kids Engaged with Creative Activities

Staying home to keep warm and stay safe? Don’t let cabin fever set in! Keep engaged and get creative with our Art with Kids @ Home program. This video series offers a variety of easy, at-home art projects you can do with kids.

Check out the videos on YouTube – you can work through the projects on the schedule and pace that works best for your family. Share your creations on social media! Tag the department and use the hashtag #ArtWithKidsAtHome.

Free Produce Markets Resume in February

Access to fresh, nutritious food is critical to health. Many families in our community are struggling to purchase food and other basic necessities. To help residents, Columbus Recreation and Parks’ free Mobile Produce Markets will resume at select community centers in February. In 2020, markets provided nearly 305,000 meals to more than 25,000 residents.

Eligible families can receive a one-week supply of fresh produced, based on the family size. The drive-thru Mobile Produce Markets are staffed by volunteers wearing masks and gloves who load the produce directly into your trunk or car. Markets are first-come, first-served and last until produce runs out.

The first free Mobile Produce Market is Feb. 4, 3 p.m. at Glenwood Community Center, 1888 Fairmont Ave., 43223.

View an updated schedule online. Follow the department on Facebook, Instagram and Twitter and follow Go, Lunch! on Facebook, Instagram and Twitter for the most up to date information.

City Council Continues to Seek Community Input on Reimagining Safety Initiative

Columbus City Council invites residents to participate in a community survey designed to gain further insight on how to establish alternative crisis response models, invest in accountability and a better Division of Police, and invest in violence prevention. 

The 16-question survey asks users for their insights into safety in Columbus and how they want to see Council advance a budget that keeps all neighborhoods safe. Access the survey online, or copy and paste the link below in your browser:  

 www.surveymonkey.com/r/ReimagineSafety

The survey is another step in Council’s commitment to reimagining public safety driven by the people. In partnership with the Saunders PR Group, residents will participate in virtual town halls, focus group discussions and hearings. The information will be quantified to inform a comprehensive safety strategy that reinvests in neighborhoods, realigns safety protocols to specific community needs while creating a more equitable Columbus.

Read more about the Columbus City Council Reimagining Safety Initiative. 

Host Your Big Day with Us

Did you get engaged this holiday season? Columbus Recreation and Parks offers a variety of wedding venues that are perfect for your big day!

We offer many indoor and outdoor venues, including shelterhouses, open air shelters and premier event venues. Learn more about the many options, including the new The Gallery at Champions. Check out the Gallery's amenities on Wedding Wire and The Knot.

Did you know several Columbus Recreation and Parks' venues were nominated for the 2021 Best of Columbus Weddings? North Bank Park Pavilion, Park of Roses and the Cultural Arts Center were nominated in this annual readers’ poll that recognizes the top vendors in dozens of wedding-related categories.

Welcome to Our New Commission Members

Columbus Recreation and Parks is excited to welcome three new commissioners, Gregg Dodd, Letha Pugh and Jamie Wilson. Each community leader was appointed by Mayor Andrew J. Ginther and approved by Columbus City Council.

The Commission, appointed and organized under the Charter of the City of Columbus, provides leadership for the Department. The group includes a cross-functional team of leaders, who leverage their diversity and commitment to social equity to guide the Department in meeting the recreational needs of residents.  

Meet the new Commissioners and learn more about this important leadership group.

It's the Season of Giving Thanks

The City of Columbus Recreation and Parks Department would like to wish a happy Thanksgiving to all of our community members! We are so grateful to be able to serve our community alongside you this year. Even though this year has included some unprecedented challenges, Thanksgiving is an opportunity for us to remember all of the blessings in our lives and to be thankful. Although we want to share in this joyous season with our family and friends, it is most important to keep everyone healthy and safe this holiday season. Please practice social distancing, avoid large gatherings, wear a mask and follow all other public health guidelines. Now is a great time to connect with others virtually to spread joy, not COVID-19. We are so thankful for all of you!

Help Your Columbus Neighbors this Holiday Season Through the Adopt-A-Center Program

Columbus Recreation and Parks Department is looking for individuals, groups and organizations to support its Adopt-a-Center program this holiday season.

The department serves thousands of seniors, adult, children and people with disabilities across 31 different community centers and programs in Columbus. Most of the centers are located in very low income neighborhoods. The public health emergency has only compounded challenges faced by poor families as many people living paycheck to paycheck find themselves unemployed with no safety net. If you, your family, or workplace can purchase a gift for a child or make a donation of any size, it will help us to brighten the holidays for these families in need. Gifts can be purchased and donations can be made through our Adopt a Center website. If your company would like to help in a bigger way, information can be found under the ‘View Sponsorship Opportunities’ at the same address.

All gifts will be distributed to the families the week of Dec. 14 so the deadline to order gifts is Dec. 4.

Please contact Erika Shemberg, Development Manager, with any questions. Thank you for considering!

Shout Out for our October Tree Planting Volunteers

Columbus Recreation and Parks Department would like to thank the various volunteer groups who helped plant trees in Hauntz Park, Wilson Road Park and Holton Park during the month of October. We appreciate your dedication to improving the environment and making Columbus' parks even more beautiful! Thank you to Subaru, CRC Consulting Services, OSU Triangle Fraternity, Columbus Gives Back, Highland West Civic Association, Gay For Good and Assent Compliance for your concerted effort and work to enhance Columbus' tree canopy! 

Volunteer Opportunity at Glenwood Produce Market

Columbus Recreation and Parks Department needs volunteers to help at the produce market event at Glenwood Community Center on Thursday, Dec. 17, from 2:30-5 p.m. Volunteers will use the PantryTrak app to look up and/or register community members, load vehicles with produce items, set up/take down tables for produce bag prep, break down boxes and dispose items. If interested, you can register for the event on VolunteerHub or contact Ruby White, Food Office Manager.

Transition to VolunteerHub

Columbus Recreation and Parks Department is utilizing the services of VolunteerHub for organizing volunteer opportunities. Be sure to create your account and volunteer profile. Check out all of our volunteer opportunities!

November 2020

Group Volunteer Opportunities

Would your corporation or organization enjoy giving back to the Columbus community? Keep volunteering with us in mind!

Check out our volunteer calendar to see new volunteer opportunities or contact Kara Johnson, Development Coordinator, for more information.

Thank you to Lowe's for donating tools that support the Columbus Recreation and Parks Department's Volunteer Program.

Department Wins Honors from OPRA

Columbus Recreation and Parks received a first place award in the Ohio Parks and Recreation Association (OPRA) Annual Awards of Excellence Program. OPRA supports parks and recreation professionals and organizations across Ohio in their efforts to provide quality facilities and recreational opportunities for all Ohioans while protecting and preserving Ohio’s natural resources. 

The award recognized the department’s efforts to address food insecurity through the Go, Lunch! free meal program and free mobile produce markets, and its efforts to connect residents with basic supplies and social services organizations with drive-through events and door-to-door canvassing. These efforts were added or adjusted to address the unique issues brought about by the pandemic. Read more about the awards program.

Receiving honors such as this underscores the department’s leadership in the industry and its commitment to improving the well-being of all residents.

Keeping Kids Active and Engaged

Columbus Recreation and Parks continues to offer programming for kids who are learning remotely, including hosting activities during the holiday break at the end of the year.

Active Learning Sites: Our 29 community centers are offering time blocks for independent school study and homework assistance. Students can bring their computer – or access a computer if needed – to complete and get assistance with schoolwork. Each community center follows the same scheduled Monday through Friday 9:30 a.m.–3 p.m. There is no cost to families. All participants must register in advance.

School’s Out: We will have activities during Winter Holiday Break 2020 for youth ages 6–12 years old. Winter break programming runs Monday, Dec. 21 through Thursday, Dec. 31 (closed Dec. 25 and Jan. 1 for the holidays). Online registration opens Monday, Dec. 7. All participants must register in advance.

The health and safety of participants and staff is our top priority. We have implemented rigorous, department-wide procedures, including daily wellness checks, a face covering requirement and social distancing protocols. Read more about these protocols.

Ulry/Warner Road Park Project Kicks Off

Do you live or work on the northeast side of Columbus? The department is asking for public input to help shape plans for a new 53-acre park at Ulry and Warner Roads.

Residents were invited to a virtual open house Nov. 10 to learn more about the project and to provide input on what would benefit their community. Residents can continue to provide input through Dec. 9 through this online survey.

Learn more about the project and share your thoughts.

City's Longest-running Artist Talks Return Virtually

The City’s longest-running series of artist talks, Conversations & Coffee, returned in a virtual format last month. Join us from the comfort of your home or office and gain key insight on art from a variety of people from different corners of the art world. Upcoming sessions include:

“D I S T A N C E” with Nicole Garlando: Loft Gallery artist Nicole “Cole” Garlando joins us at 12 p.m. on Thursday, Nov. 19 to discuss her work “D I S T A N C E” and share more of her studio practice. Join the conversation via Zoom.

“Essence of Character” with Kristin Morris: One of three current Main Gallery artists, Kristin Morris, joins us at 12 p.m. on Thursday, Dec. 3 to discuss the group exhibition “Essence of Character,” as well as individual studio practices and other upcoming projects in the works. Visit the CAC website for the link to join the Zoom meeting.

The Cultural Arts Center staff is excited to offer these lunchtime sessions after a brief hiatus due to the pandemic. Visit the CAC website for the current schedule.

Celebrate Green Friday and #OptOutside

Turn Black Friday green this year–get outside and enjoy the day!

Our friends at REI encourage everyone to #OptOutside and enjoy fresh air and family - make Nov. 27 Green Friday. Not only will you avoid the crowds, you’ll benefit from the fresh air and physical activity!

This year, Columbus Recreation and Parks is joining parks and recreation departments from across the country in a Green Friday campaign. Join the Facebook event to get ideas about things to see and do. Share your adventures on social media–use the hashtag #OptOutside and tag Columbus Recreation and Parks Department to share how you celebrate Green Friday!

Local Companies Give Back: You Can, Too!

The Adopt a Center program offers many ways to help families in need this holiday season. Whether you are a large company, a small organization or an individual, you can help!

Columbus Futsal Club has made a financial donation to the Adopt a Center effort and encouraged its members to support the effort by purchasing toys. T&M Associates, an engineering firm, has adopted a center and is encouraging other local engineering firms to join their efforts.

And many individuals have already gone to the Amazon Wish List and purchased a gift or two for a child in need.

This year has been a difficult one. Many low income adults have lost their job, resulting in families struggling to pay for basic needs. Please consider helping us to bring some holiday joy to these families. Learn how you can make a difference.
